_artifact_source: on-chfs (onchfs) on Base mainnet - recovered directly from chain state on 2026-09-28
_artifact_note: THE FALL was not stored on IPFS. Its artifact lives in the onchfs on-chain file system, and onchfs.fxhash2.xyz - the only public resolver - is dead. The artifact is nonetheless fully intact and was recovered by calling the onchfs contract directly. Every file under artifacts/the-fall/ is byte-identical to the mint.

_onchain.read_interface: getInodeAt(bytes32,string[]) / inodes(bytes32) / readDirectory(bytes32) / readFile(bytes32) / concatenateChunks(bytes32[]) - all view functions

_verification.method: Bytes were read via eth_call against the onchfs contract. Retrieval is inherently content-addressed: the inode lookup is keyed by the CID, and concatenateChunks reads each chunk from the Content Store by the keccak256 of its own content, so a chunk cannot be returned under a hash it does not match.
_verification.cross_checked_against: the copy previously served from repo source (series/screensavers/the_fall)
_verification.result: index.html, index.js and p5/p5.min.js were already byte-identical. fxhash.min.js differed by exactly one trailing newline, which was removed so the served tree is byte-identical to the mint.
_verification.styles_css: The mint contains no styles.css, but index.html requests one. That 404 was present in the minted artifact itself; it is faithful, and the page uses no CSS classes (all layout is inline).

_unrelated_dangling_reference._note: Separate from the artifact. The provenance document referenced by data.js is on IPFS and is genuinely gone.
_unrelated_dangling_reference._why: A kubo node with 431 peers queried the DHT for providers and found none, so no node on the IPFS network is providing this block. Not a gateway outage - a dangling reference.
_unrelated_dangling_reference._replacement: The on-chain inode tree above is a stronger and still-live provenance record than the lost IPFS document; the artwork's canonical content is the chain itself.
